newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise slightly on new fund hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise slightly on new fund hopes.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were buoyed on Wednesday by expectations of a fresh flow of funds though some shares flagged in late trading, operators said.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose to 359.76 from 355.35 on a slim $36.2 million total market volume.
Market leader UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3156 from Tuesday's closing $0.3140, while oil company LUKoil rose to $15.30 from $15.09.
"As a rule, stocks like LUKoil grow either when totally new money arrives, or when someone knows that it is on its way," said Sergei Sheikov, head of corporate securities at Raiffeisen Bank Austria.
Dealers noted brisk trade of second tier liquid shares, continuing a recent trend, and said increased activity on the first tier was due to new investors.
International long-distance provider Rostelekom edged up to $3.86 from $3.81, while oil company Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.877 from $0.864.

"There is certainly greater interest in blue chips today than there was yesterday," said Bank MFK head securities analyst Dmitry Konov. "Given the big and long-standing Western demand on the second tier, something had to happen in the blue chips."
Konov said interest in the leading shares was falling off, however, and forecast only a small rise in prices on Thursday.
"I expect only marginal growth, though it looks like buying will continue," he said.
